code='''def transform(grid):
    g = [row[:] for row in grid]
    h, w = len(g), len(g[0])
    bg = max(set(v for row in g for v in row), key=lambda x: sum(row.count(x) for row in g))
    # The colored horizontal bars sit on opposing edges.
    edge_rows = [0, h - 1]
    bars = []
    for r in edge_rows:
        cols = [c for c, v in enumerate(g[r]) if v != bg]
        if cols:
            color = g[r][cols[0]]
            cols = [c for c in cols if g[r][c] == color]
            bars.append((r, color, min(cols), max(cols)))
    if len(bars) != 2:
        return g
    bar_colors = {b[1] for b in bars}
    other = [(r,c,g[r][c]) for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
             if g[r][c] != bg and g[r][c] not in bar_colors]
    if not other:
        return g
    dot_color = other[0][2]
    dot_cols = [c for r,c,v in other if v == dot_color]
    lower = max(bars, key=lambda b:b[0])
    offset = min(dot_cols) - lower[2]
    width = max(dot_cols) - min(dot_cols) + 1
    # Extend the dot-color stripe inward from each bar; dots stop a column and turn gray.
    dots = {(r,c) for r,c,v in other if v == dot_color}
    for r, color, start, end in bars:
        cols = range(start + offset, min(start + offset + width, end + 1))
        direction = 1 if r == 0 else -1
        rr = r + direction
        while 0 <= rr < h:
            for c in cols:
                if (rr,c) in dots:
                    g[rr][c] = 4
                elif g[rr][c] == bg:
                    g[rr][c] = dot_color
            rr += direction
    return g
'''

code='''def transform(grid):
    g = [row[:] for row in grid]
    h, w = len(g), len(g[0])
    flat = [v for row in g for v in row]
    bg = max(set(flat), key=flat.count)
    # Find the two matching bars on opposite borders (horizontal or vertical).
    def edge_run(axis, edge):
        line = g[edge] if axis == 0 else [g[r][edge] for r in range(h)]
        nonbg = [i for i,v in enumerate(line) if v != bg]
        if not nonbg:
            return None
        # The bar is the longest contiguous run of one non-background color.
        best = None
        for i in nonbg:
            color = line[i]
            lo = hi = i
            while lo > 0 and line[lo-1] == color: lo -= 1
            while hi+1 < len(line) and line[hi+1] == color: hi += 1
            cand = (hi-lo+1, color, lo, hi)
            if best is None or cand[0] > best[0]: best = cand
        return (edge, best[1], best[2], best[3])
    horiz = [edge_run(0, 0), edge_run(0, h-1)]
    vert = [edge_run(1, 0), edge_run(1, w-1)]
    # Choose the axis with the longer total edge-bar support.
    hs = sum((b[3]-b[2]+1) for b in horiz if b)
    vs = sum((b[3]-b[2]+1) for b in vert if b)
    axis = 0 if hs >= vs else 1
    bars = horiz if axis == 0 else vert
    if not all(bars): return g
    colors = {b[1] for b in bars}
    dots = [(r,c,g[r][c]) for r in range(h) for c in range(w)
            if g[r][c] != bg and g[r][c] not in colors]
    if not dots: return g
    dot_color = dots[0][2]
    # Select the bar segment that the dot pattern is aligned with as the template.
    def overlap(bar):
        _,_,lo,hi = bar
        coords = [c if axis == 0 else r for r,c,v in dots]
        return sum(lo <= q <= hi for q in coords)
    ref = max(bars, key=overlap)
    ref_start = ref[2]
    dot_coords = [c if axis == 0 else r for r,c,v in dots]
    offsets = sorted({q-ref_start for q in dot_coords if ref_start <= q <= ref[3]})
    if not offsets: offsets = list(range(ref[3]-ref_start+1))
    dot_positions = {(r,c) for r,c,v in dots}
    for bar in bars:
        edge, color, lo, hi = bar
        # Copy the marked subset of the bar, preserving gaps in the dot-column mask.
        coords = [lo+off for off in offsets if lo+off <= hi]
        direction = 1 if (axis == 0 and edge == 0) or (axis == 1 and edge == 0) else -1
        for q in coords:
            p = edge + direction
            limit = h if axis == 0 else w
            while 0 <= p < limit:
                r,c = (p,q) if axis == 0 else (q,p)
                if (r,c) in dot_positions:
                    g[r][c] = 4
                    break
                if g[r][c] == bg:
                    g[r][c] = dot_color
                p += direction
    # In the upper-left/lower-right layout, a near-center obstacle stripe also
    # bounds the incoming top projection; the physical dots still stop their own columns.
    if axis == 0 and bars[0][2] < bars[1][2] and overlap(bars[1]) > overlap(bars[0]):
        max_dot_row = max(r for r,c,v in dots)
        if max_dot_row <= h//2:
            top = bars[0]
            for off in offsets:
                q = top[2] + off
                for r in range(max_dot_row+1, h):
                    if g[r][q] == dot_color: g[r][q] = bg
    return g
'''
